ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To degrade a free person into servitude is to impose a lower status on someone who was not bound to it; Chan speakers use the legal-social wrong as a charge of falsely diminishing what is already present.
EvidenceBody: Foyan Qingyuan calls excessive explanation 'degrading the free into servitude.' Tianyin Yuanxiu puts the charge into a reply to an elder and also denies that saying everyone possesses the matter is such degradation. Feiyin Tongrong explicitly says equating a bound being with Shakyamuni is neither degrading the free nor calling the base noble, while Yunmen Wenyan makes 'do not degrade the free' a stock counter before a blow. Huayan Shengke turns the same charge against treating Shakyamuni as awake and the assembly as not. These cases bend a status offence into an interview accusation: the named master says the proposed distinction or explanation has needlessly lowered its subject.
